registry_entry.title: Do referees flag home and away teams differently, in a way that lasts from one period to the next?
registry_entry.question: For every regular-season game from 2016 to 2023 whose schedule row names a referee, the penalty differential is the penalty yards recorded against the away team minus those against the home team (play-by-play penalty == 1, penalty_team, penalty_yards). For each referee with at least 40 such games in 2016-2020 and at least 24 in 2021-2023, take his mean differential in each window. Correlate the two means across those referees, each weighted by the smaller of his two game counts.
registry_entry.metric: weighted correlation between a referee's 2016-2020 and 2021-2023 mean penalty differential
registry_entry.rule: PASS if the lower end of the 95% bootstrap interval (resampling referees; n_resamples and seed from the protocol) is above zero. Otherwise FAIL, and Stage 6 asks nothing more of referees.
disclosures: Before this entry was written no referee or penalty value had been read. Looked at: the column names in data/nflverse_schema.json (the schedule has referee; play-by-play has penalty, penalty_team, penalty_yards), and nflreadpy's loader signatures, printed without loading any data.
The schedule names the head referee, not the crew, and crews are reshuffled between seasons. The screen asks about the referee because that is the only name the data carries.
The screen stops at 2023, so it reads nothing from the confirmation seasons.
registry_entry.expected: weak persistence or none: referees are graded and crews rotated, and whatever home edge officiating gives is league-wide and already inside Model A's home-field term
